program_scope: One source-compiled three-member All, nested helper returns with scalar captured locals, group projection and an atomic successor. Original VM, collector, IR, catalog and host are dropped. New objects load exact original return-site paths, member identities, operands, accepted values and remaining fuel from host-owned disk records.
frontier_scope: Dispatch follows original member order. Prefix lengths 0..3 and all accepted subsets give 1+2+4+8=15 cuts per host. Six receipt permutations cover empty, partial and fully accepted but unpublished collectors. External concurrent execution orders are not tested.
ownership_scope: Parent Vm::restore_pending_in_scope and PreparedParallelSession::restore_in_scope borrow one ScopedLocalExecution owner. Parent denial, child denial/revocation and explicit post-restore cancellation close the owner, cancel retained parent/collector state and leave ledger bytes unchanged. No dispatch or successor follows these refusals.
receipt_scope: Accepted values are revalidated through PendingReply; settled but unaccepted rows use recorded replies; only unsettled effects dispatch. Stale parent/member and duplicate member receipts retain their buffers. Ordered results hand off once, and terminal checkpoint replay leaves the ledger unchanged. Host ledger policy owns deduplication, not the VM.
budget_scope: Each of 30 host/frontier combinations resumes at uninterrupted completion-cost minus one, exact cost and plus one. Outcomes and remaining fuel match the original compiler/evaluator/collector pipeline without charging preparation again or refilling parent fuel.
correspondence_scope: For each host/frontier, six altered top-level fields plus truncated and oversized candidates refuse before reconstruction against trusted committed fixture bytes. Neither the committed image nor ledger is authenticated by this fixture.
remaining_boundaries: Sequential disk recovery and captured predecessor graph composition.
General graph checkpoint ownership/codec acceptance and explicit host storage contract.
Process restart, effect-to-receipt crash consistency and final independent repository/distribution acceptance.
